paper_metadata.title: Quantum Ensemble Optimisation: Revolutionizing Investment Portfolio Management with QAOA and VQE Integration

summary: The paper studies a 3-asset portfolio optimization problem using historical Yahoo data for SPOT, META, and MSFT from 2021–2022, with risk factor 0.5, a maximum of 2 shares per company, a minimum spend of $500, and a maximum budget of $750. It compares a classical NumPyEigenSolver baseline against QAOA, VQE, and a QAOA+VQE ensemble, reporting that QAOA and the ensemble recommend one share each of SPOT, META, and MSFT, while the classical baseline recommends one share each of SPOT and META.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization experiment comparing classical NumPyEigenSolver baseline, QAOA, VQE, and an ensemble of QAOA+VQE on three real stocks (SPOT, META, MSFT); only the gate-based QAOA, VQE, and ensemble results are extracted here.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Ensemble Optimisation (QEO) combining QAOA and VQE

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Portfolio allocation over three assets; binary decision variables correspond to share-purchase choices, but the paper does not specify the exact qubit-to-variable mapping.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Portfolio optimization balancing risk and return; exact mathematical objective not provided in the paper.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Budget and share-count constraints enforced via problem setup; no explicit penalty formulation reported.

problem_instance.description: Investment portfolio optimization over three stocks using historical market data.
problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Historical stock prices were collected and a covariance matrix was computed; no further preprocessing details reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Results compared across classical NumPyEigenSolver, QAOA, VQE, and ensemble outputs; qualitative comparison based on diversification and probability distribution of optimal portfolio sampling.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Historical price data collection and covariance matrix computation.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of recommended portfolios and probability distributions; qualitative assessment of diversification and optimal-solution likelihood.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper makes qualitative claims that QAOA and the ensemble outperform classical and VQE solutions, but it does not report asymptotic speedup, runtime speedup, or complexity bounds.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No qubit count, circuit depth, shot count, or runtime data are reported; only a 3-asset toy portfolio is studied.
limiting_factors: No complexity or asymptotic speedup analysis
Only 3 assets, so problem size is very small
Comparison is qualitative rather than benchmarked with runtime or approximation ratios
No evidence of practical quantum advantage over classical baseline

notes: Hardware type is not explicitly named; Qiskit is mentioned and no annealer/QPU device is specified, so hardware is not specified rather than inferred to a specific backend.
Number of qubits, circuit depth, shots, and variational-parameter counts are not reported in the paper.
The paper reports qualitative superiority of QAOA/ensemble over classical and VQE solutions, but no asymptotic complexity or proven speedup order is given.
The paper claims the QAOA/ensemble approach is preferable and samples the optimal solution with higher probability, but it does not provide runtime, scaling, or complexity evidence.
The study is a small portfolio instance with 3 stocks, so Hoefler-style practical advantage is not demonstrated.

experiments.description: Classical baseline portfolio optimization using NumPyEigenSolver on the same 3-asset instance (SPOT, META, MSFT) with risk factor 0.5, max 2 shares per company, minimum spending $500, and maximum budget $750.
key_results: Classical solution recommends buying one share each of SPOT and META.
Used as the baseline against QAOA, VQE, and the ensemble model.
